facts.fact: The World Bank's Digital Economy Assessment states that all public and faith-based hospitals and health centres use DHIS2, which holds integrated data on HIV, infectious diseases, reproductive health, nutrition and surveillance for all health regions, districts and hospitals; it gives no date, so the 2020 publication year is used.

The World Bank's Digital Economy Assessment states that health centres and hospitals enter their data themselves directly in DHIS2, most having IT equipment and connectivity with occasional connectivity problems; it gives no date, so the 2020 publication year is used.

The World Bank's Digital Economy Assessment states that all public and faith-based health centres use DHIS2 and enter their data themselves, while saying only that most have equipment and connectivity; it gives no numerator, denominator or date, so the 2020 publication year is used.

The World Bank's Digital Economy Assessment states that DHIS2 is one of the key aspects of the health ministry's PNDIS, which it calls an advanced strategy with a clear roadmap; the 2020 publication year is used.

The World Bank's Digital Economy Assessment states that Open Clinic, which manages patients' administrative and medical files under a unique patient identification number, is available in 23 hospitals (15 public and 8 privately run), without giving their level; no date is given, so the 2020 publication year is used.

The World Bank's Digital Economy Assessment states that Open Clinic is to be extended to 14 more hospitals by June 2022 with the support of Enabel and the EU, leaving ten unconnected; the 2020 publication year is used.

The World Bank's Digital Economy Assessment states that Open Clinic is one of the key aspects of the health ministry's PNDIS, which it calls an advanced strategy with a clear roadmap; the 2020 publication year is used.
